{{Ship module infobox}}

The '''Sub-surface Displacement Missile''' is a mining hardpoint that drills into a targeted sub-surface asteroid deposit and detonates a shaped charge at the pilot's command. A correctly timed detonation ejects commodity fragments for collection and refining.<ref name="frontier-recap">[https://forums.frontier.co.uk/threads/content-recap-beyond-chapter-four-livestream-mining-and-squadrons.454587/ Content Recap: Beyond – Chapter Four Livestream – Mining and Squadrons], Frontier Developments, 1 November 2018.</ref>

The launcher is specific to [[Sub-surface Mining|sub-surface mining]]. It does not identify deposits, collect the released fragments, or process them. Those roles belong to the [[Prospector Limpet Controller]], [[Collector Limpet Controller]], and [[Refinery]].

== Variants and specifications ==

The standard launcher is B-rated and is available in Class 1 or Class 2, with fixed and turreted mounts. Class 2 carries three times the ammunition of Class 1 but requires a medium hardpoint and twice the mass.<ref name="missile">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Sub-surface_Displacement_Missile Sub-surface Displacement Missile], Elite Dangerous Wiki.</ref>

A turreted launcher functions as a full turret only when controlled by a Multicrew gunner. For a solo pilot it behaves as a forward-fired tool, so mount position and alignment with the moving deposit remain important.<ref name="missile" />

== Target and drilling behavior ==

A prospector limpet reveals a suitable feature as a named '''Sub-surface Deposit'''. With that deposit targeted, the launcher is fired while the trigger remains held. The missile flies straight; if it strikes the deposit, it begins drilling into the asteroid.<ref name="missile" />

The drilling display then shows a progress marker moving across a changing density graph while blue extraction bands move in the opposite direction. Releasing the trigger detonates the shaped charge. A release while the marker overlaps a blue band ejects material; a release outside a band does not produce the intended fragment.<ref name="subsurface-guide">[https://edmining.com/sub-surface-mining/ Elite Dangerous: Sub Surface Mining], ED Mining.</ref>

Rock density changes the drill's progress rate, so the release cannot be timed from a fixed count. The live marker and the approaching blue band must be read on every shot. [[How to Sub-surface Mine]] covers the full timing procedure.

== Deposit depletion ==

Each successful or failed drilling attempt damages the deposit and reduces the amount that remains available. A deposit can be drilled repeatedly until it is depleted, but the number and placement of extraction bands vary.<ref name="missile" />

The launcher ejects fragments rather than finished cargo. Collector limpets or a cargo scoop must recover them, and a refinery must process their commodity content before it enters the cargo hold.

== Failure states ==

* '''The missile does not start drilling:''' confirm that a prospector is attached, target a revealed sub-surface deposit, use Analysis Mode, and strike the deposit rather than ordinary asteroid surface.
* '''No fragment is ejected:''' the trigger was released outside a blue extraction band. Watch the live marker rather than relying on a fixed delay.
* '''The marker changes speed unexpectedly:''' the drill has entered rock of different density; adjust the release point to the current rate.
* '''The deposit disappears or stops accepting shots:''' it has been depleted by repeated attempts.
* '''The launcher will not fire:''' check the active fire group, Analysis Mode, ammunition, module power, and whether the single-round clip is reloading.
* '''Shots repeatedly miss:''' reduce relative motion, approach a slower-spinning deposit, or reposition so the hardpoint has a clear line of fire.

== Selection and fitting ==

Class 1 preserves a medium hardpoint and is adequate when sub-surface deposits are an occasional target. Class 2 is better suited to a dedicated session because its 96-round capacity reduces the risk of exhausting ammunition, but it does not remove the need to time each shot correctly.

One launcher is normally sufficient. Sub-surface extraction is limited by alignment, the drilling sequence, deposit depletion, collection, and refinery throughput rather than by simultaneous missile fire.

A practical fit also needs a prospector controller, collector support, a refinery, cargo space, and limpets. Shields and responsive thrusters help while matching the rotation of an irregular asteroid at close range.

== Method boundaries ==

A displacement missile works only on a prospector-revealed sub-surface deposit. It cannot cut ordinary asteroid fragments, dislodge exposed surface deposits, or crack fissured cores. Those targets require a [[Mining Laser]], [[Abrasion Blaster]], or [[Seismic Charge Launcher]] respectively.

== Engineering ==

The Sub-surface Displacement Missile does not accept ordinary Engineer blueprints.

== Field Procedure ==

[[How to Sub-surface Mine]] covers prospecting, approach geometry, aiming, interpreting the density graph, release timing, repeated extraction, collection, and troubleshooting. [[Sub-surface Mining]] explains the method and its relationship to other forms of asteroid mining.
